column1: 7 - Beginning with Fiscal Year 2023, NIH converted the manual categories of Minority Health and Health Disparities into four automated categories to enhance accuracy and better distinguish research funding from workforce development and capacity building funding. The new automated categories are 1) Health Disparities Research, 2) Racial and Ethnic Minority Health Research, 3) Health Disparities and Racial or Ethnic Minority Health Research, and 4) Building Research Capacity at Institutions with Limited NIH Funding. The Health Disparities Research category is not restricted to the populations with health disparities, as designated by the NIMHD director. The category Health Disparities and Racial or Ethnic Minority Health Research reflects the union of the first two individual categories with duplicate projects removed. The new category Building Research Capacity at Institutions with Limited NIH Funding captures projects designed to enhance and build research capabilities for resource limited institutions with $25 million or less in NIH research funding or $50 million or less in total NIH funding, as well as projects for resource limited states (e.g., IDeA), federally recognized Tribes and Tribal Organizations, and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU). Since manual and automated figures are not comparable, the historical funding numbers for the two manual categories will no longer be posted here but are available upon request by contacting rcdc@mail.nih.gov.

More information on HIV/AIDS and HIV/AIDS-related research is available at https://www.oar.nih.gov/hiv-policy-and-research.

column1: 12 - Reporting for the Underage Drinking - Prevention & Treatment (NIAAA Only) category does not follow the standard RCDC process. Spending for this category is reported consistent with U.S. Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP) requirements. This category includes only projects funded and administered by NIAAA. This category represents a subset of spending reported under the RCDC Underage Drinking category and involves manual review of the project listing by subject matter experts. Actuals or estimates displayed in RePORT can differ from levels identified in the Drug Control budget submission to ONDCP for those fiscal years where either comparable, rounding or other adjustments have been applied or historical data was refined.

column1: 14 - Estimates of United States disease burden are provided as mortality and prevalence figures for calendar year 2024. Figures for mortality data are drawn from the  National Vital Statistics System (NVSS), and indicate the number of deaths in which a particular disease or condition was mentioned on a deceased individual's death certificate. Prevalence figures are drawn from National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) responses and report the percentage of respondents who indicated that they were affected by a particular health condition. Standard error, a measure of the uncertainty in the estimate, is presented in parentheses alongside the prevalence estimate. Estimates of mortality and prevalence are not available for all NIH spending categories. Further descriptions of these disease statistics can be found here.
